_readme: The Road Here (V1.16, November 2026: John's consolidated copy; Road Here paragraphs may carry several **bold** phrases, approved per paragraph. Earlier: V1.7 build, October 2026; Phase 3A scaffold): every word on the page, section by section. **text** is set in bold (one phrase a paragraph at most); `accent` is the headline phrase in the accent color. No numbered eyebrows or chapter navigation (V1.7). Images are asset ids in assets.json (road-*). Privacy: the band is never named, linked or described in identifying detail anywhere on this page or in its metadata. V1.8: the milestone bar and the festival caption are removed; the hero portrait is a transparent cutout. V1.13: operator.groups carry a short label (the collapsed card) and a title that begins with it (the open card adds the rest), plus an icon (each card's large, faint, cropped graphic); each timeline milestone names its outline icon (Icon.astro). V1.15: school.stage is Section 2's image group: the live performance photograph as the dominant base, with John's three supplied transparent prints (festival poster, television still, artist credential) laid over its corners, each in a named slot (upper-right, lower-left, lower-right).

meta.title: The Road Here
meta.description: Before Web3, John Cowin spent over a decade turning an original music project into a professional touring operation, and managing the day-to-day operations behind it.

hero.headline: Before Web3. There was music.
hero.copy: Before Web3, I spent **over a decade** turning an original music project into a **professional touring operation**. What started behind a drum kit grew into an education in entrepreneurship, marketing, partnerships, creative work, and managing day-to-day operations.

school.headline: From practice rooms to national stages.
paragraphs: I studied **music performance, business, and media**, then put that training to work building an original music project from the ground up.

What began with local shows grew into **more than a decade as a professional musician**. Along the way, I played **major festivals**, appeared on television and FM radio, earned an endorsement from an instrument manufacturer, and secured **worldwide distribution through a Sony Music subsidiary**.

operator.headline: On stage at night. Running the business by day.
operator.copy: Before **professional management and distribution** came on board, I **managed much of the day-to-day operation myself**. After signing those deals, I **remained deeply involved** across touring, marketing, partnerships, logistics, and release coordination.

pivot.headline: Then 2020 happened.
paragraphs: After years of near-constant touring, I was ready for a life with more time at home. Then COVID brought live music to a stop.

Around the same time, I **discovered DeFi**, and **the potential clicked immediately**. I immersed myself in the technology, began investing, joined communities, and built relationships the same way I had in music: by showing up and contributing. That led to my **first professional role in Web3**.

timeline.what: Studied music performance, business, and media
Secured worldwide distribution through a Sony Music subsidiary
Discovered DeFi and began studying the technology

led.headline: Different industry. Same operating instincts.
led.copy: Music taught me to **go deep in a craft** without losing sight of how the whole operation worked. Along the way, I learned that **audiences are earned**, **relationships compound**, and ideas are only as valuable as the execution behind them. I bring that same **range, depth, and follow-through** to Web3.

pairs.now: Event activations, logistics, and on-site production
Social content, community growth, and engagement
